newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines gets extra U.S. sugar quota.
newsitem.headline: Philippines gets extra U.S. sugar quota.

text.p: The Philippines has been granted an additional sugar quota of 27,411 tonnes by the United States for the 1996/97 crop year ending August, the Sugar Regulatory Administration said on Wednesday.
The SRA chief Wilson Gamboa told reporters at a news conference the original U.S. allocation to the Philippines for the current crop year was 219,000 tonnes.
The U.S. imports sugar from some countries at a premium over world prices.
The extra quota to the Philippines comes at a time when the country's sugar millers are saddled with large quantities of unsold stocks.
Gamboa told reporters Philippine millers had unsold stocks of 100,000 tonnes in warehouses.

Last week, the country's biggest sugar miller Victorias Milling Co reported problems in repaying debts of 4.423 billion pesos ($168 million). The company blamed its financial troubles on a glut in the local sugar market.
